summary: Stefania Travagnin is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. She held a post at the University of Groningen (~2013–2019) and took up a position at SOAS University of London around 2020.

Stefano Zacchetti (1968–2020) specialized in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his PhD at Ca' Foscari University of Venice under Alfredo Cadonna, and held posts at Soka University (2001–2012) and the University of Oxford (~2012–2020).

Stella Kramrisch (1896–1993) was an Indologist and historian-archaeologist. After studying at the University of Vienna (~1914–1919), she held academic positions at the University of Calcutta (~1923–1950) and the University of Pennsylvania (~1950–1972).

Sten Konow (1867–1948) was an Indologist and linguist who earned his doctorate under Richard Pischel. His career included posts at the University of Oslo (1896–1899, 1910), Archaeological Survey of India (1906–1908), and University of Hamburg (1914–1919).
Stephan Beyer is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Richard Hugh Robinson. He held a professorship at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested 1977).
Stephan Marcus Salzberg is a Sinology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of British Columbia (attested 1983) under Yoshitaka Iriya, Shoko Kanaoka, and Daniel L. Overmyer.

Stephanie Kaza is a religious and Buddhist studies scholar. She completed a Ph.D. in biology at UC Santa Cruz and an M.Div. at Starr King School for the Ministry, later serving as Professor of Environmental Studies at the University of Vermont (~1991–2015).
Stephanie Roemer is a scholar in the field of Tibetology. She completed her doctoral studies under supervisors Eberhard Sandschneider and Toni Huber.

Stephanie W. Jamison (born 1948) is an Indologist and linguist who studied at Yale (~1969–1977). She held appointments at Harvard (~1986–1989) and became Professor of Sanskrit and Indo-Iranian Linguistics at UCLA around 2002.

Stephen Addiss (1935–2022) was a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and art history. He earned his Ph.D. from the University of Michigan and held professorships at the University of Kansas (~1977–1992) and the University of Richmond (~1992–2013).

Stephen Batchelor (born 1953) is a Buddhist studies scholar and philosopher. He studied under traditional teachers Ngawang Dhargyey, Geshe Rabten, and Kusan Sunim, and held a post at Songgwangsa from 1981 to 1984.

Stephen C. Berkwitz is a religious and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Kelaniya (1995–1997). He has served as Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Missouri State University.

Stephen F. Teiser (born 1956) is a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar. He completed his PhD at Princeton University (~1978–1986), taught at Middlebury College (~1986–1988), and was appointed D.T. Suzuki Professor in Buddhist Studies at Princeton (~1988).

Stephen G. Covell (born 1965) specializes in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He completed doctoral studies under Jacqueline I. Stone at Princeton University (~1996–2001) and joined Western Michigan University around 2003.

Stephen H. West (born 1944) is a Sinologist who studied at the University of Michigan (~1968–1972). He served as Professor of East Asian Languages at UC Berkeley (~1986–2003) and later held a post at Arizona State University (~2003).

Stephen J. Laumakis works in philosophy and Buddhist studies, having studied under John Kronen, Ramdas Lamb, and George J. Tanabe, Jr. He served as Professor of Philosophy at the University of St. Thomas (attested 2013).

Stephen L. Jenkins (1953–2016) was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Harvard under Masatoshi Nagatomi and Charles Hallisey, and later served as Professor of Religious Studies at California State Polytechnic University, Humboldt (attested 2010–2013).

Stephen Prothero (born 1960) is a religious studies scholar. He completed degrees at Yale University (~1978–1982) and Harvard University (~1986–1990), and has held a post at Boston University since approximately 1996.

Stephen R. Bokenkamp (born 1949) is a Sinologist and religious studies scholar educated at UC Berkeley (~1976–1986). He served on the faculty at Indiana University (~1989–2007) and Arizona State University (~2007).
Stephen Suen is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his PhD at the University of Hong Kong under the supervision of K. L. Dhammajoti (attested 2009).
